Let \( a_0, a_1, a_2, \ldots \) be the unique sequence of nonnegative integers less than 397 with \( a_0 = 1 \) and

\[ a_{n+1}(a_n + 1)^2 \equiv a_n \pmod{397} \]

for all nonnegative integers \( n \). Given that \( a_{2026} = 9 \), compute the remainder when \( a_0 + a_1 + \cdots + a_{2026} \) is divided by 397.

Put your final answer within \boxed{}.

message.content:
Let all congruences be modulo \(397\). Since \(a_{2026}=9\neq 0\), none of \(a_0,\dots,a_{2026}\) can be \(0\); otherwise the sequence would stay \(0\). Also \(397\) is prime, so these terms are invertible.

Define

\[
b_n \equiv a_n^{-1}\pmod{397}.
\]

From

\[
a_{n+1}(a_n+1)^2 \equiv a_n,
\]

take reciprocals:

\[
a_{n+1}^{-1} \equiv a_n^{-1}(a_n+1)^2.
\]

Thus

\[
b_{n+1} \equiv b_n(a_n+1)^2
= b_n(a_n^2+2a_n+1)
\equiv a_n+2+b_n.
\]

So

\[
a_n \equiv b_{n+1}-b_n-2.
\]

Now sum from \(n=0\) to \(2026\):

\[
\sum_{n=0}^{2026} a_n
\equiv b_{2027}-b_0-2\cdot 2027.
\]

We have \(b_0=a_0^{-1}=1\). Also \(a_{2026}=9\), so

\[
b_{2026}=9^{-1}\pmod{397}.
\]

Since \(9\cdot 44=396\equiv -1\), we get \(9^{-1}\equiv -44\equiv 353\). Therefore

\[
b_{2027}\equiv b_{2026}+2+a_{2026}
\equiv 353+2+9
=364.
\]

Finally,

\[
2\cdot 2027=4054\equiv 84\pmod{397}.
\]

Hence

\[
\sum_{n=0}^{2026} a_n
\equiv 364-1-84
=279\pmod{397}.
\]

\[
\boxed{279}
\]
